question: What is C# and what platform is it primarily used on?
options: A high-level, object-oriented programming language primarily used on the .NET platform.
A scripting language primarily used on the Java platform.
A low-level assembly language used for embedded systems.
A functional language primarily used on the Python platform.
correctAnswer: A high-level, object-oriented programming language primarily used on the .NET platform.
explanation: C# is a modern, object‑oriented language designed by Microsoft for building applications on the .NET platform.

question: What is the difference between value types and reference types in C#?
options: Value types store data directly on the stack, while reference types store a reference to data on the heap.
Value types are always nullable, whereas reference types cannot be null.
Value types are defined only in C#, while reference types are defined only in Java.
Value types are allocated on the heap, and reference types are allocated on the stack.
correctAnswer: Value types store data directly on the stack, while reference types store a reference to data on the heap.
explanation: In C#, value types contain the actual data and are typically allocated on the stack; reference types hold a pointer to an object stored on the heap.

question: What is the .NET Framework?
options: A Windows-only, full-featured implementation of the .NET runtime that includes libraries, CLR, and tools.
An open-source, cross-platform runtime that replaces the CLR.
A database management system for .NET applications.
A front-end UI framework for building web applications.
correctAnswer: A Windows-only, full-featured implementation of the .NET runtime that includes libraries, CLR, and tools.
explanation: The .NET Framework is Microsoft's original, Windows‑only implementation that bundles the CLR, Base Class Library, and development tools.

question: What is .NET Core and how does it differ from the .NET Framework?
options: .NET Core is a cross‑platform, modular, open‑source implementation of .NET, whereas the .NET Framework is Windows‑only and monolithic.
.NET Core is a proprietary extension of the .NET Framework that only runs on Linux.
.NET Core is a visual designer tool, while the .NET Framework is a programming language.
.NET Core is the same as the .NET Framework but with a different name.
correctAnswer: .NET Core is a cross‑platform, modular, open‑source implementation of .NET, whereas the .NET Framework is Windows‑only and monolithic.
explanation: .NET Core was created to run on Windows, Linux, and macOS, offering a modular runtime, unlike the Windows‑only, monolithic .NET Framework.

question: What is the Common Language Runtime (CLR)?
options: The virtual machine component of .NET that manages execution, memory, and services like garbage collection.
A compiler that translates C# code directly to machine code without any runtime.
A database engine used by .NET applications to store data.
A UI library for creating Windows Forms applications.
correctAnswer: The virtual machine component of .NET that manages execution, memory, and services like garbage collection.
explanation: The CLR is the runtime environment that loads, executes, and provides services such as memory management, type safety, and garbage collection for .NET applications.

question: What is the difference between C# and Java?
options: C# is compiled to native machine code while Java is interpreted
C# runs on the .NET CLR and Java runs on the JVM
C# supports multiple inheritance of classes while Java does not
C# uses pointers extensively whereas Java does not
correctAnswer: C# runs on the .NET CLR and Java runs on the JVM
explanation: C# code is executed by the .NET Common Language Runtime, whereas Java code runs on the Java Virtual Machine.

question: What is a namespace in C#?
options: A way to organize classes and other types into a hierarchical container
A keyword to import external assemblies
A method to manage memory allocation
A feature that enables unsafe code blocks
correctAnswer: A way to organize classes and other types into a hierarchical container
explanation: Namespaces group related types and prevent naming collisions.

question: What is the purpose of the using directive in C#?
options: It imports types from a namespace so they can be referenced without full qualification
It declares a variable of type using
It defines a new namespace
It enables garbage collection for the imported types
correctAnswer: It imports types from a namespace so they can be referenced without full qualification
explanation: The using directive allows you to use types without specifying their full namespace each time.

question: What is the Main method in a C# program?
options: The entry point of a C# program where execution begins
A method that must be static and must return a string
A method that can be called from any class without an instance
A method that is automatically executed after the program terminates
correctAnswer: The entry point of a C# program where execution begins
explanation: Main is the required entry point; the runtime starts execution from this method.

question: What is the difference between int and Int32 in C#?
options: int is an alias for System.Int32, both represent a 32-bit signed integer
int is a value type while Int32 is a reference type
int is only available in unsafe code, Int32 is not
int is 64-bit on 64-bit platforms, Int32 is always 32-bit
correctAnswer: int is an alias for System.Int32, both represent a 32-bit signed integer
explanation: In C#, int is simply a language keyword that maps to the System.Int32 struct.

question: What is a class in C#?
options: A blueprint that defines the structure and behavior of objects.
A variable that holds a single value.
A method that returns a value.
An interface that cannot contain implementation.
correctAnswer: A blueprint that defines the structure and behavior of objects.
explanation: A class serves as a template for creating objects, specifying their data members and methods.

question: What is an object in C#?
options: A compiled assembly file.
An instance of a class or struct that contains data and behavior.
A namespace that groups related classes.
A delegate that points to a method.
correctAnswer: An instance of a class or struct that contains data and behavior.
explanation: An object is created from a class or struct and holds its own state and can invoke its behavior.

question: What is the difference between a class and a struct in C#?
options: Classes are reference types stored on the heap, while structs are value types stored on the stack.
Classes can inherit from other classes, but structs can inherit from multiple interfaces.
Structs support default parameterless constructors, whereas classes do not.
Both classes and structs are reference types.
correctAnswer: Classes are reference types stored on the heap, while structs are value types stored on the stack.
explanation: Classes are reference types allocated on the heap; structs are value types typically allocated on the stack and copied by value.

question: What is a constructor in C#?
options: A special method that is called automatically to initialize a new object.
A property that gets or sets a field value.
A static method used to create instances.
An event handler for object disposal.
correctAnswer: A special method that is called automatically to initialize a new object.
explanation: Constructors run when an object is instantiated, allowing initialization of its fields.

question: What is a default constructor in C#?
options: A constructor that takes parameters for all fields.
A parameterless constructor automatically provided by the compiler if no other constructors are defined.
A static constructor that initializes static members.
A private constructor that prevents object creation.
correctAnswer: A parameterless constructor automatically provided by the compiler if no other constructors are defined.
explanation: If a class defines no constructors, C# supplies a public parameterless constructor that initializes fields to their default values.

question: What is method overloading in C#?
options: Defining multiple methods with same name but different parameter lists within the same class.
Redefining a base class method in a derived class with same signature.
Using the 'override' keyword to change method behavior at runtime.
Declaring a method as virtual to allow polymorphism.
correctAnswer: Defining multiple methods with same name but different parameter lists within the same class.
explanation: Method overloading allows several methods to share a name as long as their parameter signatures differ, enabling compile‑time polymorphism.

question: What is method overriding in C#?
options: Declaring multiple methods with same name but different return types.
Providing a new implementation of a virtual or abstract method in a derived class using the 'override' keyword.
Using method overloading to achieve polymorphism.
Marking a method as static to hide base class method.
correctAnswer: Providing a new implementation of a virtual or abstract method in a derived class using the 'override' keyword.
explanation: Overriding replaces the base class's virtual/abstract method with a new implementation in the derived class, using the 'override' keyword.

question: What is the difference between var and dynamic in C#?
options: 'var' is implicitly typed at compile time, while 'dynamic' bypasses compile-time type checking and is resolved at runtime.
'var' can only be used for primitive types, 'dynamic' for reference types.
'var' requires explicit type declaration, 'dynamic' does not.
Both are the same; they are just aliases.
correctAnswer: 'var' is implicitly typed at compile time, while 'dynamic' bypasses compile-time type checking and is resolved at runtime.
explanation: 'var' lets the compiler infer the type and enforce it; 'dynamic' defers type resolution to runtime, allowing operations that are not checked at compile time.

question: What is the purpose of the const keyword in C#?
options: To declare a field whose value can be changed only within the constructor.
To define a compile-time constant whose value cannot be changed after compilation.
To allow a variable to be assigned only once at runtime.
To create a read-only property.
correctAnswer: To define a compile-time constant whose value cannot be changed after compilation.
explanation: A const field must be assigned a value at declaration and is baked into the assembly; it cannot be altered at runtime.

question: What is the difference between const and readonly in C#?
options: const values are set at runtime, readonly at compile time.
const fields must be assigned at declaration and are compile-time constants; readonly fields can be assigned in declaration or constructor and are runtime constants.
const can be used with reference types, readonly cannot.
readonly fields can be modified after object creation, const cannot.
correctAnswer: const fields must be assigned at declaration and are compile-time constants; readonly fields can be assigned in declaration or constructor and are runtime constants.
explanation: const is a compile‑time constant; readonly can be set either at declaration or within a constructor, allowing different values per instance while still being immutable after construction.

question: What is boxing and unboxing in C#?
options: Boxing is converting a value type to an object type; unboxing extracts the value type from the object.
Boxing copies a reference type to the heap; unboxing moves it back to the stack.
Boxing encrypts a string; unboxing decrypts it.
Boxing and unboxing are synonyms for serialization and deserialization.
correctAnswer: Boxing is converting a value type to an object type; unboxing extracts the value type from the object.
explanation: Boxing wraps a value type in an object, and unboxing retrieves the original value type from that object.

question: What is the difference between == and .Equals() in C#?
options: == compares reference equality for reference types (or value equality for value types), while .Equals() can be overridden to provide custom value equality.
== always calls .Equals() internally, so they behave identically.
.Equals() compares memory addresses, whereas == compares the content of strings only.
== works only with numeric types, while .Equals() works only with objects.
correctAnswer: == compares reference equality for reference types (or value equality for value types), while .Equals() can be overridden to provide custom value equality.
explanation: .Equals() can be overridden to define what equality means for a type, while == uses the default reference or value comparison.

question: What are access modifiers in C#?
options: They are keywords that control the visibility of types and members, such as public, private, protected, internal, and protected internal.
They are attributes that automatically generate getters and setters for properties.
They are compiler directives that enable or disable garbage collection.
They are methods that encrypt and decrypt class fields at runtime.
correctAnswer: They are keywords that control the visibility of types and members, such as public, private, protected, internal, and protected internal.
explanation: Access modifiers define how and where a type or member can be accessed from other code.

question: What is the difference between public, private, and protected access modifiers?
options: public is accessible from any code, private only within the containing type, protected within the containing type and derived types.
public can be accessed only within the same assembly, private across all assemblies, protected only by static methods.
public and protected are identical, while private hides the member from the compiler.
public members are read‑only, private members are write‑only, protected members are both.
correctAnswer: public is accessible from any code, private only within the containing type, protected within the containing type and derived types.
explanation: These three modifiers define the scope of accessibility: public everywhere, private inside the class, protected inside the class and its subclasses.

question: What is inheritance in C#?
options: Inheritance allows a class to derive from a base class, acquiring its members and enabling polymorphism.
Inheritance merges two unrelated classes into a single namespace.
Inheritance is a way to copy methods from one class to another at runtime.
Inheritance automatically creates a singleton instance of a class.
correctAnswer: Inheritance allows a class to derive from a base class, acquiring its members and enabling polymorphism.
explanation: Through inheritance, a derived class reuses code from a base class and can override or extend its behavior.

question: What is polymorphism in C#?
options: The ability of a class to inherit from multiple base classes.
The ability of objects to be treated as instances of their base type, allowing methods to be overridden or overloaded.
The process of hiding data members from other classes.
The mechanism that enforces access restrictions on class members.
correctAnswer: The ability of objects to be treated as instances of their base type, allowing methods to be overridden or overloaded.
explanation: Polymorphism lets a derived class be used wherever its base class is expected, enabling method overriding and overloading.

question: What is encapsulation in C#?
options: Allowing a class to inherit from multiple interfaces.
Bundling data and methods together in a class and restricting direct access from outside.
Defining methods without implementation.
Creating multiple forms of a method with the same name.
correctAnswer: Bundling data and methods together in a class and restricting direct access from outside.
explanation: Encapsulation groups related data and behavior and hides the internal state behind public members.

question: What is abstraction in C#?
options: Providing multiple implementations of the same method.
Hiding complex implementation details and exposing only essential features.
Restricting access to class members using access modifiers.
Allowing a class to inherit from multiple base classes.
correctAnswer: Hiding complex implementation details and exposing only essential features.
explanation: Abstraction focuses on exposing only what is necessary, often via abstract classes or interfaces, while hiding the rest.

question: What is an interface in C#?
options: A class that can be instantiated directly.
A contract that defines method signatures without implementation, which classes can implement.
A class that provides default implementations for all its members.
A sealed class that cannot be inherited.
correctAnswer: A contract that defines method signatures without implementation, which classes can implement.
explanation: An interface specifies a set of members that implementing classes must provide, without containing implementation itself.

question: What is the difference between an abstract class and an interface in C#?
options: Abstract classes can be instantiated directly, interfaces cannot.
Abstract classes can contain fields and concrete methods; interfaces originally could only contain method signatures, and a class can inherit from multiple interfaces but only one abstract class.
Interfaces support multiple inheritance, abstract classes do not support inheritance at all.
Both abstract classes and interfaces can be instantiated, but only interfaces support properties.
correctAnswer: Abstract classes can contain fields and concrete methods; interfaces originally could only contain method signatures, and a class can inherit from multiple interfaces but only one abstract class.
explanation: Abstract classes may have implementations and state, while interfaces define only contracts; C# allows multiple interface implementations but single class inheritance.

question: What is a property in C#?
options: A member that provides a flexible mechanism to read, write, or compute the value of a private field.
A method that can be called without an instance.
A class that inherits from System.Object.
A namespace used to organize code.
correctAnswer: A member that provides a flexible mechanism to read, write, or compute the value of a private field.
explanation: A property encapsulates access to a field, allowing get and/or set logic while keeping the field private.

question: What is the difference between a field and a property in C#?
options: Fields store data directly; properties expose data through get/set accessors.
Fields can have get/set; properties cannot.
Fields are always static; properties are always instance.
Fields are defined in interfaces; properties are not.
correctAnswer: Fields store data directly; properties expose data through get/set accessors.
explanation: Fields are simple storage variables, while properties provide controlled access via accessor methods.

question: What are auto-implemented properties in C#?
options: Properties where the compiler automatically creates a hidden backing field.
Properties that must be manually coded with a private field.
Methods that automatically implement interfaces.
Delegates that auto-bind to events.
correctAnswer: Properties where the compiler automatically creates a hidden backing field.
explanation: Auto-implemented properties let the compiler generate the backing field, reducing boilerplate code.

question: What is the this keyword used for in C#?
options: Refers to the current instance of the class.
Refers to the base class of the current class.
Creates a new thread.
Imports a namespace.
correctAnswer: Refers to the current instance of the class.
explanation: 'this' provides a reference to the object whose member is being accessed, useful for disambiguation.

question: What is the base keyword used for in C#?
options: Used to access members of the base class from a derived class.
Used to create a new instance of a class.
Used to define a static method.
Used to reference the current object.
correctAnswer: Used to access members of the base class from a derived class.
explanation: 'base' allows a derived class to call constructors or members defined in its immediate base class.

question: What is a static class in C#?
options: A class that can only contain static members and cannot be instantiated.
A class that can be instantiated multiple times but shares state across instances.
A class that inherits from System.Object and overrides its methods.
A class that is automatically garbage collected after each method call.
correctAnswer: A class that can only contain static members and cannot be instantiated.
explanation: A static class cannot be instantiated and may contain only static members; it is sealed and serves as a container for related static members.

question: What is a static method in C#?
options: A method that belongs to an instance of a class and can access instance fields.
A method that can be called without creating an instance of its class and can only access static members.
A method that must be declared inside a static class.
A method that is executed asynchronously by default.
correctAnswer: A method that can be called without creating an instance of its class and can only access static members.
explanation: Static methods belong to the type itself, not to any object, so they can be invoked via the class name and may only reference other static members.

question: What is the difference between static and instance members in C#?
options: Static members are shared across all instances of a class, while instance members belong to each individual object.
Static members can only be used in console applications, instance members only in web apps.
Static members are stored on the heap, instance members on the stack.
Static members can be overridden, instance members cannot.
correctAnswer: Static members are shared across all instances of a class, while instance members belong to each individual object.
explanation: Static members have a single copy per type, accessible without an object; instance members exist separately for each object instance.

question: What is an array in C#?
options: A fixed-size collection of elements of the same type stored contiguously in memory.
A dynamic list that automatically resizes as elements are added.
A key-value pair collection similar to a dictionary.
A type that can only hold primitive data types.
correctAnswer: A fixed-size collection of elements of the same type stored contiguously in memory.
explanation: C# arrays have a predetermined length set at creation and store elements of a single type in a contiguous block.

question: What is the difference between an array and a List in C#?
options: Arrays have a fixed size after creation, while List<T> can grow or shrink dynamically.
Arrays support LINQ queries, while List<T> does not.
Arrays are reference types, while List<T> is a value type.
Arrays can store elements of different types, List<T> cannot.
correctAnswer: Arrays have a fixed size after creation, while List<T> can grow or shrink dynamically.
explanation: Arrays are of fixed length once allocated; List<T> is a generic collection that can add or remove items, resizing internally as needed.

question: What is a string in C#, and is it a value type or reference type?
options: A sequence of Unicode characters; it is a reference type.
A sequence of Unicode characters; it is a value type.
A numeric type representing characters; it is a value type.
A collection of bytes; it is a reference type.
correctAnswer: A sequence of Unicode characters; it is a reference type.
explanation: In C#, string represents a sequence of Unicode characters and is implemented as a reference type.

question: What is string immutability in C#?
options: Once created, the contents of a string cannot be changed; operations produce a new string.
Strings can be modified in place without creating a new object.
String immutability means strings are stored on the stack.
It allows strings to be garbage collected immediately after use.
correctAnswer: Once created, the contents of a string cannot be changed; operations produce a new string.
explanation: String objects are immutable; any modification results in a new string instance.

question: What is the difference between String and StringBuilder in C#?
options: String is immutable, while StringBuilder is mutable and designed for frequent modifications.
StringBuilder is immutable, while String is mutable.
Both are immutable, but StringBuilder uses less memory.
StringBuilder can only be used with numeric data.
correctAnswer: String is immutable, while StringBuilder is mutable and designed for frequent modifications.
explanation: StringBuilder allows efficient in‑place modifications, whereas String creates a new object for each change.

question: What is a nullable type in C#?
options: A value type that can also hold the value null, declared with a trailing '?'
A reference type that cannot hold null.
A type that automatically converts null to default value.
A type that only works with strings.
correctAnswer: A value type that can also hold the value null, declared with a trailing '?'
explanation: Nullable types (e.g., int?) enable value types to represent null in addition to their normal range.

question: What is the null-coalescing operator (??) in C#?
options: It returns the left-hand operand if it is not null; otherwise, it returns the right-hand operand.
It checks if both operands are null and throws an exception.
It concatenates two strings, treating null as empty.
It converts a null value to zero.
correctAnswer: It returns the left-hand operand if it is not null; otherwise, it returns the right-hand operand.
explanation: The ?? operator provides a fallback value when the left expression evaluates to null.

question: What is the null-conditional operator (?.) in C#?
options: It allows safe navigation of members and elements, returning null instead of throwing a NullReferenceException.
It forces a compile-time error when a null value is accessed.
It is used to declare nullable value types.
It converts a value type to a reference type.
correctAnswer: It allows safe navigation of members and elements, returning null instead of throwing a NullReferenceException.
explanation: The null-conditional operator (?.) lets you access members or elements safely; if the left-hand operand is null, the whole expression evaluates to null rather than throwing a NullReferenceException.

question: What is exception handling in C# and what keywords are used?
options: A mechanism to handle runtime errors using the keywords try, catch, finally, and throw.
A way to prevent compile-time errors using the keywords if, else, switch.
A method to serialize objects using the keywords serialize, deserialize.
A technique to manage memory using the keywords new, delete.
correctAnswer: A mechanism to handle runtime errors using the keywords try, catch, finally, and throw.
explanation: Exception handling in C# uses try to enclose risky code, catch to handle specific exceptions, finally for cleanup, and throw to raise exceptions.

question: What is the difference between throw and throw ex in C#?
options: throw rethrows the original exception preserving the stack trace, while throw ex creates a new exception losing the original stack trace.
throw ex rethrows the original exception preserving the stack trace, while throw creates a new exception.
Both throw and throw ex behave identically.
throw is used only for System.Exception, while throw ex is for custom exceptions.
correctAnswer: throw rethrows the original exception preserving the stack trace, while throw ex creates a new exception losing the original stack trace.
explanation: Using plain throw preserves the original stack trace; using throw ex (or throw e) resets the stack trace because it treats it as a new throw.

question: What is a try-catch-finally block used for in C#?
options: To execute code that may throw exceptions, handle them, and run cleanup code regardless of success.
To define a loop that repeats until a condition is met.
To declare a class and its members.
To perform asynchronous operations.
correctAnswer: To execute code that may throw exceptions, handle them, and run cleanup code regardless of success.
explanation: The try block contains code that might throw, catch blocks handle specific exceptions, and the finally block runs cleanup code irrespective of whether an exception occurred.

question: What is the purpose of the finally block in exception handling?
options: It contains code that runs after the try and any catch blocks, regardless of whether an exception was thrown.
It catches exceptions that were not caught by previous catch blocks.
It rethrows the caught exception automatically.
It defines the type of exception to be thrown.
correctAnswer: It contains code that runs after the try and any catch blocks, regardless of whether an exception was thrown.
explanation: The finally block is guaranteed to execute after try/catch, making it ideal for releasing resources such as file handles or database connections.

question: What is LINQ in C# and how is it used?
options: LINQ (Language Integrated Query) is a set of query operators that allows querying collections using a SQL‑like syntax directly in C# code.
LINQ is a third‑party library that replaces the .NET collections framework.
LINQ is a debugging tool that visualizes memory usage of objects at runtime.
LINQ is a compiler directive that automatically generates unit tests for methods.
correctAnswer: LINQ (Language Integrated Query) is a set of query operators that allows querying collections using a SQL‑like syntax directly in C# code.
explanation: LINQ integrates query capabilities into C#, letting developers write declarative queries against in‑memory collections, databases, XML, etc., using familiar syntax.

question: What is async/await in C# and how does it work?
options: async marks a method as asynchronous and await pauses the method until the awaited Task completes without blocking the thread.
async and await are keywords that automatically parallelize any loop in C# code.
async converts a method into a background thread, while await forces the method to run on the UI thread.
async/await are attributes used to mark methods for remote procedure calls.
correctAnswer: async marks a method as asynchronous and await pauses the method until the awaited Task completes without blocking the thread.
explanation: The async modifier enables the use of await inside a method; await yields control until the awaited Task finishes, allowing non‑blocking asynchronous execution.

question: What is the difference between IEnumerable and IQueryable in C#?
options: IEnumerable executes queries locally in memory, while IQueryable builds an expression tree that can be translated and executed by a remote provider such as a database.
IEnumerable can only be used with arrays, whereas IQueryable works only with List<T>.
IEnumerable supports parallel execution by default, whereas IQueryable does not support parallelism.
IEnumerable returns results as JSON, while IQueryable returns results as XML.
correctAnswer: IEnumerable executes queries locally in memory, while IQueryable builds an expression tree that can be translated and executed by a remote provider such as a database.
explanation: IEnumerable performs in‑memory iteration; IQueryable defers execution and allows providers (e.g., Entity Framework) to translate the query to the underlying data source language.

question: What are delegates and events in C#?
options: A delegate is a type‑safe function pointer, and an event is a special delegate member that provides a publish‑subscribe mechanism with controlled access.
A delegate is a class that stores data, while an event is a method that runs automatically on object creation.
A delegate is a keyword for multithreading, and an event is a keyword for exception handling.
A delegate is a UI component, and an event is a CSS style applied to it.
correctAnswer: A delegate is a type‑safe function pointer, and an event is a special delegate member that provides a publish‑subscribe mechanism with controlled access.
explanation: Delegates encapsulate method references; events expose delegate invocation only to the declaring class, enabling other classes to subscribe without invoking directly.

question: What is the difference between a delegate and an event in C#?
options: A delegate is a type that defines a method signature, while an event is a language construct that wraps a delegate to restrict external invocation.
A delegate can only reference static methods, whereas an event can reference instance methods.
A delegate automatically runs on a separate thread, while an event runs on the UI thread.
A delegate stores data in a database, while an event logs messages to the console.
correctAnswer: A delegate is a type that defines a method signature, while an event is a language construct that wraps a delegate to restrict external invocation.
explanation: Delegates describe callable signatures; events use those delegates but enforce encapsulation, allowing only the declaring class to raise the event.

question: What is a lambda expression in C#?
options: An inline, anonymous function that can contain expressions or statements and can be used wherever a delegate type is expected
A named method defined inside a class
A keyword that creates a new thread
A way to serialize objects to JSON
correctAnswer: An inline, anonymous function that can contain expressions or statements and can be used wherever a delegate type is expected
explanation: A lambda expression is a concise way to write an anonymous function that can be assigned to a delegate or expression tree.

question: What is an anonymous method in C#?
options: A method without a name defined using the delegate keyword, introduced in C# 2.0, allowing inline delegate creation
A static method that cannot be overridden
A lambda expression that returns void
A method that is automatically generated by the compiler for async operations
correctAnswer: A method without a name defined using the delegate keyword, introduced in C# 2.0, allowing inline delegate creation
explanation: Anonymous methods let you write an inline block of code that matches a delegate signature without declaring a separate named method.

question: What is the difference between Func, Action, and Predicate delegates?
options: Func returns a value and can have up to 16 input parameters; Action returns void and can have up to 16 input parameters; Predicate is a specialized Func that takes one input and returns a bool
Func and Action are interchangeable; Predicate is only used with LINQ
Func always takes exactly one parameter, Action always takes exactly two, Predicate takes three
All three are identical except for naming conventions
correctAnswer: Func returns a value and can have up to 16 input parameters; Action returns void and can have up to 16 input parameters; Predicate is a specialized Func that takes one input and returns a bool
explanation: Func<T,..., TResult> produces a result, Action<T,...> returns void, and Predicate<T> is defined as Func<T,bool> for boolean tests.

question: What is the difference between IEnumerable and IList in C#?
options: IEnumerable provides read‑only forward iteration; IList adds indexing, Count, and allows modification of elements
IEnumerable allows random access while IList only supports sequential access
IEnumerable is mutable, IList is immutable
IEnumerable is a concrete class, IList is an interface
correctAnswer: IEnumerable provides read‑only forward iteration; IList adds indexing, Count, and allows modification of elements
explanation: IEnumerable<T> only supports simple iteration, whereas IList<T> inherits from ICollection<T> and adds indexers and mutability.

question: What is deferred execution in LINQ?
options: The query is not executed when defined but when its results are enumerated, allowing the underlying data to change before execution
The query runs on a background thread automatically
The query results are cached after the first execution
The query is compiled into SQL before execution
correctAnswer: The query is not executed when defined but when its results are enumerated, allowing the underlying data to change before execution
explanation: Deferred execution means a LINQ query builds an expression tree and runs only when you iterate over it, reflecting any changes made to the source collection.

question: What is the difference between LINQ to Objects and LINQ to SQL?
options: LINQ to Objects works with in‑memory collections, while LINQ to SQL translates queries to SQL for relational databases.
LINQ to Objects can only query XML, while LINQ to SQL works with JSON.
LINQ to Objects requires a database connection, LINQ to SQL does not.
LINQ to Objects uses deferred execution, LINQ to SQL always executes immediately.
correctAnswer: LINQ to Objects works with in‑memory collections, while LINQ to SQL translates queries to SQL for relational databases.
explanation: LINQ to Objects operates on in‑memory data structures (arrays, List<T>, etc.), whereas LINQ to SQL converts the query into SQL statements that run against a relational database.

question: What is the yield keyword used for in C#?
options: To create an iterator block that returns elements one at a time using lazy evaluation.
To allocate memory on the heap.
To define a lambda expression.
To mark a method as asynchronous.
correctAnswer: To create an iterator block that returns elements one at a time using lazy evaluation.
explanation: The yield keyword enables a method to return each element of a sequence on demand, implementing lazy iteration via IEnumerable/IEnumerator.

question: What is an extension method in C#?
options: A static method that appears as an instance method on an existing type, defined in a static class with a "this" parameter.
A method that can only be used inside the same assembly.
A method that overrides a base class method.
A method that must be declared as abstract.
correctAnswer: A static method that appears as an instance method on an existing type, defined in a static class with a "this" parameter.
explanation: Extension methods are static methods in static classes that use the "this" modifier on the first parameter, allowing them to be called as if they were instance methods on the extended type.

question: What is generics in C# and why are they used?
options: Generics allow type‑safe data structures and methods without casting, improving performance and compile‑time checking.
Generics are used to encrypt data.
Generics enable dynamic typing at runtime.
Generics replace the need for interfaces.
correctAnswer: Generics allow type‑safe data structures and methods without casting, improving performance and compile‑time checking.
explanation: Generics provide compile‑time type safety, eliminate the need for boxing/unboxing or explicit casts, and enable reusable, efficient code.

question: What is the difference between generic and non‑generic collections in C#?
options: Generic collections enforce compile‑time type safety and avoid boxing/unboxing, while non‑generic collections store objects and require casting.
Generic collections are slower than non‑generic collections.
Non‑generic collections support LINQ, generic collections do not.
Generic collections cannot be enumerated.
correctAnswer: Generic collections enforce compile‑time type safety and avoid boxing/unboxing, while non‑generic collections store objects and require casting.
explanation: Generic collections (e.g., List<T>) keep the element type known at compile time, preventing runtime casting and boxing, whereas non‑generic collections (e.g., ArrayList) store items as objects, requiring casts and incurring boxing overhead.

question: What is the difference between List<T> and Dictionary<TKey, TValue>?
options: List<T> stores elements in a key-value pair, while Dictionary<TKey,TValue> stores a simple ordered list.
List<T> is an ordered collection accessed by index; Dictionary<TKey,TValue> is an unordered collection accessed by a unique key.
List<T> allows duplicate keys, Dictionary<TKey,TValue> does not allow duplicate values.
List<T> is thread‑safe by default, Dictionary<TKey,TValue> is not.
correctAnswer: List<T> is an ordered collection accessed by index; Dictionary<TKey,TValue> is an unordered collection accessed by a unique key.
explanation: List<T> maintains element order and is accessed by zero‑based index, whereas Dictionary<TKey,TValue> stores key‑value pairs and lookup is done via the unique key, without guaranteed order.

question: What is the difference between an interface and an abstract class in terms of multiple inheritance?
options: A class can implement multiple interfaces but can inherit from only one abstract class.
A class can inherit from multiple abstract classes but can implement only one interface.
Both interfaces and abstract classes support multiple inheritance equally.
Interfaces cannot contain method signatures, while abstract classes can.
correctAnswer: A class can implement multiple interfaces but can inherit from only one abstract class.
explanation: C# allows a class to implement any number of interfaces, but it can inherit from only a single base class, whether abstract or concrete.

question: What is the purpose of the sealed keyword in C#?
options: Prevents a class from being instantiated.
Allows a class to be inherited only once.
Prevents a class from being inherited.
Marks a method as abstract.
correctAnswer: Prevents a class from being inherited.
explanation: Applying sealed to a class stops other classes from deriving from it, effectively ending the inheritance chain.

question: What is the difference between overloading and overriding in C#?
options: Overloading changes method behavior at runtime; overriding changes it at compile time.
Overloading defines multiple methods with same name but different signatures; overriding provides a new implementation of a virtual method in a derived class.
Overloading can only be used with constructors; overriding can only be used with properties.
Overloading requires the base class to be sealed; overriding requires the method to be static.
correctAnswer: Overloading defines multiple methods with same name but different signatures; overriding provides a new implementation of a virtual method in a derived class.
explanation: Overloading is compile‑time polymorphism using different parameter lists; overriding is runtime polymorphism where a derived class replaces a virtual base method.

question: What is the virtual keyword used for in C#?
options: To declare a method that cannot be overridden.
To indicate that a method is abstract and must be implemented in derived classes.
To allow a method to be overridden in a derived class.
To make a class sealed.
correctAnswer: To allow a method to be overridden in a derived class.
explanation: Marking a method as virtual enables derived classes to provide their own implementation using the override keyword.

question: What is the override keyword used for in C#?
options: To hide a base class member with a new implementation
To provide a new implementation of a virtual or abstract method in a derived class
To declare a static method
To enforce compile‑time type safety
correctAnswer: To provide a new implementation of a virtual or abstract method in a derived class
explanation: override replaces the base class's virtual/abstract method with a new implementation in the derived class.

question: What is method hiding using the new keyword in C#?
options: It replaces the base class method at runtime
It creates a new overload with different parameters
It hides a base class member with the same signature, requiring the new keyword
It makes the method abstract
correctAnswer: It hides a base class member with the same signature, requiring the new keyword
explanation: The new keyword tells the compiler that the derived member intentionally hides an inherited member with the same name/signature.

question: What is the difference between shallow copy and deep copy in C#?
options: Shallow copy duplicates only value‑type fields, deep copy duplicates both value‑type and reference‑type fields recursively
Shallow copy copies the object reference, deep copy copies the reference and creates new instances of referenced objects
Shallow copy creates a new object with all fields copied, deep copy only copies the top‑level fields
There is no difference; both terms mean the same
correctAnswer: Shallow copy duplicates only value‑type fields, deep copy duplicates both value‑type and reference‑type fields recursively
explanation: A shallow copy copies field values as‑is, so reference fields still point to the same objects; a deep copy clones those referenced objects as well.

question: What is serialization and deserialization in C#?
options: Serialization converts an object to a JSON string, deserialization converts a CSV file to an object
Serialization transforms an object into a format that can be stored or transmitted, deserialization reconstructs the object from that format
Serialization encrypts data, deserialization decrypts it
Serialization only works with XML, deserialization only works with binary
correctAnswer: Serialization transforms an object into a format that can be stored or transmitted, deserialization reconstructs the object from that format
explanation: Serialization writes an object's state to a stream (JSON, XML, binary, etc.); deserialization reads that stream to recreate the object.

question: What is the difference between JSON serialization and XML serialization in C#?
options: JSON serialization preserves type information automatically, while XML does not
JSON produces a text format that is generally more compact and easier to read, whereas XML includes explicit tags and can represent schema information
XML serialization can only serialize public fields, JSON can serialize private fields
JSON serialization requires the DataContract attribute, XML does not
correctAnswer: JSON produces a text format that is generally more compact and easier to read, whereas XML includes explicit tags and can represent schema information
explanation: JSON is lighter and more human‑readable; XML is verbose with tags and can embed schema (XSD) details.

question: What is reflection in C#?
options: A way to inspect and modify metadata about assemblies, types, and members at runtime.
A compile-time feature that enforces type safety.
A garbage collection algorithm.
A syntax for defining delegates.
correctAnswer: A way to inspect and modify metadata about assemblies, types, and members at runtime.
explanation: Reflection enables runtime inspection of types, members, and attributes, allowing dynamic invocation and metadata access.

question: What is the purpose of attributes in C#?
options: To provide metadata that can be attached to code elements and retrieved at compile time or runtime.
To increase execution speed of methods.
To replace interfaces.
To handle exceptions automatically.
correctAnswer: To provide metadata that can be attached to code elements and retrieved at compile time or runtime.
explanation: Attributes store declarative information about program elements that can be examined via reflection.

question: What is a custom attribute in C#?
options: A user-defined class derived from System.Attribute that can be applied to program elements to store custom metadata.
A built-in attribute provided by .NET.
A method that overrides ToString.
A delegate type for event handling.
correctAnswer: A user-defined class derived from System.Attribute that can be applied to program elements to store custom metadata.
explanation: Custom attributes are created by inheriting from System.Attribute, allowing developers to attach their own metadata.

question: What is the difference between Task and async Task in C#?
options: Task is the type representing an asynchronous operation, while async Task is a method modifier indicating the method runs asynchronously and returns a Task.
Task is used only for CPU‑bound work, async Task only for I/O‑bound work.
Task automatically starts on a new thread, async Task runs on the UI thread.
There is no difference; they are interchangeable.
correctAnswer: Task is the type representing an asynchronous operation, while async Task is a method modifier indicating the method runs asynchronously and returns a Task.
explanation: `Task` is the return type; `async` marks a method as asynchronous and enables `await` inside it, returning a Task.

question: What is the difference between Task.Run() and Task.Factory.StartNew()?
options: Task.Run schedules work on the thread pool with default options and is simpler; Task.Factory.StartNew provides more overloads and can customize task creation options.
Task.Run creates a new thread, while StartNew uses the thread pool.
Task.Run can only be used with async methods, StartNew cannot.
Task.Run returns void, StartNew returns Task.
correctAnswer: Task.Run schedules work on the thread pool with default options and is simpler; Task.Factory.StartNew provides more overloads and can customize task creation options.
explanation: Task.Run is a convenience wrapper for common scenarios, whereas StartNew offers fine‑grained control over scheduling and task options.

question: What is a ConfigureAwait(false) used for in async programming?
options: It forces the continuation to run on the original synchronization context
It prevents capturing the current synchronization context, allowing the continuation to run on any thread
It makes the async method execute synchronously
It automatically retries the operation on failure
correctAnswer: It prevents capturing the current synchronization context, allowing the continuation to run on any thread
explanation: ConfigureAwait(false) tells the awaiter not to capture the current synchronization context, so the continuation can run on a thread-pool thread instead of, for example, the UI thread.

question: What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous programming in C#?
options: Synchronous code blocks the calling thread until the operation finishes; asynchronous code allows the thread to continue while the operation runs in the background
Synchronous code always runs on multiple cores, while asynchronous code runs on a single core
Synchronous code requires the async keyword, whereas asynchronous code does not
Synchronous code uses the lock keyword, while asynchronous code uses ConfigureAwait
correctAnswer: Synchronous code blocks the calling thread until the operation finishes; asynchronous code allows the thread to continue while the operation runs in the background
explanation: In synchronous programming the thread waits for the operation to complete; asynchronous programming releases the thread to do other work and resumes when the operation completes.

question: What is a race condition and how can it be avoided in C#?
options: It occurs when multiple threads access shared data without proper synchronization; it can be avoided by using locking mechanisms such as the lock statement
It occurs when a thread sleeps for too long; it can be avoided by removing Thread.Sleep calls
It occurs only with async/await; it can be avoided by always using ConfigureAwait(true)
It occurs when LINQ queries are executed in parallel; it can be avoided by calling ToList() first
correctAnswer: It occurs when multiple threads access shared data without proper synchronization; it can be avoided by using locking mechanisms such as the lock statement
explanation: A race condition happens when threads compete to read/write shared state without coordination; using lock, Mutex, or other synchronization primitives ensures exclusive access.

question: What is the lock keyword used for in C#?
options: To create a new thread
To synchronize access to a critical section, ensuring only one thread executes it at a time
To serialize an object to JSON
To mark a method as asynchronous
correctAnswer: To synchronize access to a critical section, ensuring only one thread executes it at a time
explanation: The lock statement acquires a mutual-exclusion lock on a given object, preventing other threads from entering the protected block until the lock is released.

question: What is thread safety and why is it important?
options: It means code can be executed by multiple threads simultaneously without causing race conditions or corrupting shared data, which is essential for correctness in concurrent applications
It means the code runs faster on multi‑core CPUs
It means the code always uses the lock keyword
It means the code cannot use async/await
correctAnswer: It means code can be executed by multiple threads simultaneously without causing race conditions or corrupting shared data, which is essential for correctness in concurrent applications
explanation: Thread‑safe code guarantees correct behavior when accessed by multiple threads, preventing data races, crashes, and inconsistent state.

question: What is the difference between Monitor and Mutex in C#?
options: Monitor works only within a single process, while Mutex can be used across multiple processes.
Monitor is a .NET class, Mutex is a C++ construct.
Monitor provides thread pooling, Mutex provides thread scheduling.
Monitor is used for I/O operations, Mutex for CPU-bound tasks.
correctAnswer: Monitor works only within a single process, while Mutex can be used across multiple processes.
explanation: Monitor is limited to synchronization within the same process, whereas Mutex can synchronize across process boundaries.

question: What is the purpose of the volatile keyword in C#?
options: It ensures that a field is compiled to a constant value.
It prevents the compiler and CPU from reordering reads/writes to the field, ensuring the latest value is always read.
It makes the field thread-safe for all operations.
It allows the field to be accessed only within the declaring class.
correctAnswer: It prevents the compiler and CPU from reordering reads/writes to the field, ensuring the latest value is always read.
explanation: volatile tells the runtime that the field may be modified by multiple threads, so reads/writes cannot be cached or reordered.

question: What is dependency injection and why is it useful?
options: A design pattern where objects are created inside the class that uses them, improving encapsulation.
A technique to pass dependencies to a class via constructors, properties, or methods, promoting loose coupling and testability.
A method of encrypting data before injection into a database.
A way to inject SQL queries directly into C# code.
correctAnswer: A technique to pass dependencies to a class via constructors, properties, or methods, promoting loose coupling and testability.
explanation: DI externalizes the creation of dependent objects, making code more modular, easier to test, and reducing coupling.

question: What is the difference between constructor injection and property injection?
options: Constructor injection supplies dependencies through the class constructor, guaranteeing they are available when the object is created; property injection sets dependencies via public settable properties after construction.
Constructor injection uses static fields, property injection uses instance fields.
Constructor injection is only for value types, property injection only for reference types.
Constructor injection requires reflection, property injection does not.
correctAnswer: Constructor injection supplies dependencies through the class constructor, guaranteeing they are available when the object is created; property injection sets dependencies via public settable properties after construction.
explanation: Constructor injection ensures required dependencies are provided at creation time, while property injection allows optional or mutable dependencies to be set later.

question: What is the Repository pattern and how is it used in C#?
options: A pattern that provides a collection-like interface for accessing data sources, abstracting data access logic and allowing swapping of data stores.
A pattern that enforces a singleton instance for database connections.
A pattern that automatically generates SQL queries from LINQ expressions.
A pattern that stores objects in memory without any persistence.
correctAnswer: A pattern that provides a collection-like interface for accessing data sources, abstracting data access logic and allowing swapping of data stores.
explanation: The Repository pattern abstracts data access behind a consistent interface, making the data layer interchangeable and easier to unit‑test.

question: What is the Singleton design pattern and how is it implemented in C#?
options: A pattern that ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it, typically implemented using a private static field, a private constructor, and a public static property that returns the instance, optionally using lazy initialization and thread‑safety mechanisms.
A pattern that creates multiple instances of a class based on input parameters, using a static factory method.
A pattern that separates an object’s construction from its representation, allowing the same construction process to create different representations.
A pattern that allows an object to change its behavior when its internal state changes.
correctAnswer: A pattern that ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it, typically implemented using a private static field, a private constructor, and a public static property that returns the instance, optionally using lazy initialization and thread‑safety mechanisms.
explanation: The Singleton guarantees a single instance and is implemented in C# with a private static instance, private constructor, and a public static accessor, often with lazy and thread‑safe initialization.

question: What is the Factory design pattern in C#?
options: A pattern that provides an interface for creating families of related or dependent objects without specifying their concrete classes, typically using a factory method that returns an interface or abstract class.
A pattern that ensures a class has only one instance throughout the application.
A pattern that allows an object to be accessed as if it were a collection.
A pattern that caches frequently accessed data to improve performance.
correctAnswer: A pattern that provides an interface for creating families of related or dependent objects without specifying their concrete classes, typically using a factory method that returns an interface or abstract class.
explanation: The Factory pattern abstracts object creation, letting client code work with interfaces or base types while the concrete class is chosen inside the factory method.

question: What is the difference between ADO.NET and Entity Framework?
options: ADO.NET is a low‑level data access technology that works with DataReaders, DataSets, and manual SQL, while Entity Framework is an ORM that maps database tables to .NET objects and lets you query with LINQ.
ADO.NET is an object‑relational mapper, whereas Entity Framework is a low‑level API for executing raw SQL commands.
Both ADO.NET and Entity Framework are the same; they provide identical functionality.
Entity Framework is used only for NoSQL databases, while ADO.NET works only with relational databases.
correctAnswer: ADO.NET is a low‑level data access technology that works with DataReaders, DataSets, and manual SQL, while Entity Framework is an ORM that maps database tables to .NET objects and lets you query with LINQ.
explanation: ADO.NET provides direct, manual data access; Entity Framework builds on it to offer object‑relational mapping and LINQ‑based queries.

question: What is a connection string in ADO.NET?
options: A text string that contains the information required to establish a connection to a data source, such as server name, database name, authentication details, and provider.
A C# class that represents a database table in code.
A method that executes a stored procedure.
A configuration file that stores UI layout settings.
correctAnswer: A text string that contains the information required to establish a connection to a data source, such as server name, database name, authentication details, and provider.
explanation: The connection string supplies all parameters needed for ADO.NET to open a database connection.

question: What is the difference between DataSet and DataReader in ADO.NET?
options: DataSet is a disconnected, in‑memory representation of data that can hold multiple tables and relationships, while DataReader provides a fast, forward‑only, read‑only stream of data directly from the database.
DataReader stores data in XML format, whereas DataSet stores data in binary format.
DataSet can only retrieve one row at a time, while DataReader can retrieve the entire result set at once.
DataReader automatically maps database columns to C# properties, whereas DataSet requires manual mapping.
correctAnswer: DataSet is a disconnected, in‑memory representation of data that can hold multiple tables and relationships, while DataReader provides a fast, forward‑only, read‑only stream of data directly from the database.
explanation: DataSet allows complex, disconnected manipulation of multiple tables; DataReader is optimized for fast, sequential read‑only access.

question: What is the difference between Entity Framework and Entity Framework Core?
options: EF is the original .NET Framework ORM, while EF Core is a cross‑platform, lightweight rewrite that runs on .NET Core and .NET 5+.
EF Core supports lazy loading, while EF does not.
EF can only be used with SQL Server, EF Core works with any database.
EF Core is a visual designer tool, EF is code‑only.
correctAnswer: EF is the original .NET Framework ORM, while EF Core is a cross‑platform, lightweight rewrite that runs on .NET Core and .NET 5+.
explanation: EF targets the full .NET Framework and is older; EF Core is a newer, cross‑platform, modular version designed for .NET Core and later.

question: What is a migration in Entity Framework Core?
options: A way to generate SQL scripts that update the database schema to match the current model.
A method to seed initial data into the database.
A feature that automatically creates indexes for foreign keys.
A tool for profiling query performance.
correctAnswer: A way to generate SQL scripts that update the database schema to match the current model.
explanation: Migrations capture model changes and produce SQL to bring the database schema in sync with the code model.

question: What is the difference between eager loading and lazy loading in Entity Framework?
options: Eager loading loads related data immediately with the main query; lazy loading defers loading until the navigation property is accessed.
Eager loading uses stored procedures; lazy loading uses LINQ.
Eager loading works only with one‑to‑many relationships; lazy loading works only with one‑to‑one.
Eager loading requires DbContext, lazy loading does not.
correctAnswer: Eager loading loads related data immediately with the main query; lazy loading defers loading until the navigation property is accessed.
explanation: Eager loading uses Include/ThenInclude to fetch related entities in one query, while lazy loading fetches them on demand via proxies.

question: What is the difference between code-first and database-first approaches in Entity Framework?
options: Code‑first starts from C# classes and generates the database; database‑first starts from an existing database and generates C# classes.
Code‑first can only target SQL Server; database‑first works with any provider.
Code‑first does not support migrations; database‑first does.
Code‑first requires a visual designer; database‑first uses only code.
correctAnswer: Code‑first starts from C# classes and generates the database; database‑first starts from an existing database and generates C# classes.
explanation: Code‑first defines the model in code and lets EF create the schema; database‑first reverse‑engineers an existing schema into model classes.

question: What is the purpose of the DbContext class in Entity Framework?
options: It represents a session with the database, allowing querying and saving of entity instances.
It defines the database connection string only.
It provides UI components for data entry.
It compiles LINQ queries into stored procedures automatically.
correctAnswer: It represents a session with the database, allowing querying and saving of entity instances.
explanation: DbContext is the primary class for interacting with the database: tracking changes, executing queries, and persisting data.

question: What is the garbage collector in .NET and how does it work?
options: It is an automatic memory management service that frees memory occupied by objects that are no longer reachable, using a generational, mark-and-sweep algorithm.
It is a manual tool that developers must invoke to release unmanaged resources after each use.
It compiles C# code into native machine code at runtime to improve performance.
It encrypts all objects in memory to protect them from being read by other processes.
correctAnswer: It is an automatic memory management service that frees memory occupied by objects that are no longer reachable, using a generational, mark-and-sweep algorithm.
explanation: The .NET GC automatically tracks object references and reclaims memory of objects that are no longer reachable, using generational collections and a mark‑and‑sweep process.

question: What is dependency injection in ASP.NET Core?
options: A design pattern that provides objects their dependencies through constructors or services, managed by the built‑in IoC container.
A way to hard‑code service instances directly inside controllers for better performance.
A technique to serialize objects into JSON for HTTP responses.
A method to encrypt configuration files at startup.
correctAnswer: A design pattern that provides objects their dependencies through constructors or services, managed by the built‑in IoC container.
explanation: ASP.NET Core includes a built‑in IoC container; dependency injection supplies required services to classes via constructors, promoting loose coupling.

question: Explain the Entity Framework Core lifecycle.
options: It includes the states: Added, Unchanged, Modified, Deleted, and Detached, and transitions occur when calling Add, Update, Remove, SaveChanges, etc.
It runs a continuous background thread that syncs the database every second regardless of changes.
It only supports a single state called "Persistent" for all entities.
It automatically generates stored procedures for every LINQ query at compile time.
correctAnswer: It includes the states: Added, Unchanged, Modified, Deleted, and Detached, and transitions occur when calling Add, Update, Remove, SaveChanges, etc.
explanation: EF Core tracks entity objects through these states; calling methods like Add or SaveChanges moves entities between states, determining how changes are persisted.

question: What is the difference between Task and Thread in C#?
options: A Task represents an asynchronous operation that may run on a thread‑pool thread, whereas a Thread is a low‑level OS thread created explicitly.
A Task is always executed on the UI thread, while a Thread can only run background work.
A Task consumes more memory than a Thread because it stores the entire call stack twice.
A Thread can only be used in .NET Framework, while Task is exclusive to .NET Core.
correctAnswer: A Task represents an asynchronous operation that may run on a thread‑pool thread, whereas a Thread is a low‑level OS thread created explicitly.
explanation: Tasks are higher‑level abstractions that schedule work on the thread pool; Threads are OS resources created directly, making Tasks more lightweight for async code.

question: Explain the generational garbage collection model used in .NET.
options: The GC divides the managed heap into Generation 0, 1, and 2, collecting younger generations more frequently; objects that survive promotions move to older generations.
It stores all objects in a single flat heap and collects the entire heap on every GC cycle.
It uses three separate physical memory devices for each generation to improve cache locality.
It only collects Generation 2 objects, leaving Generation 0 and 1 untouched.
correctAnswer: The GC divides the managed heap into Generation 0, 1, and 2, collecting younger generations more frequently; objects that survive promotions move to older generations.
explanation: .NET's generational GC optimizes performance by collecting short‑lived objects in Gen 0 often, promoting survivors to older generations that are collected less often.

question: What is the difference between Gen0, Gen1, and Gen2 garbage collection in .NET?
options: Gen0 is the youngest generation collected most frequently; Gen1 holds objects that survived Gen0; Gen2 is the oldest generation collected least frequently
Gen0 is used for large objects, Gen1 for small objects, and Gen2 for pinned objects
Gen0 stores stack allocations, Gen1 stores heap allocations, and Gen2 stores the Large Object Heap
Gen0 manages unmanaged memory, Gen1 manages managed memory, and Gen2 manages both
correctAnswer: Gen0 is the youngest generation collected most frequently; Gen1 holds objects that survived Gen0; Gen2 is the oldest generation collected least frequently
explanation: Gen0 is the first generation where new objects are allocated and collected quickly; survivors move to Gen1, and long‑lived objects end up in Gen2, which is collected far less often.

question: What is the finalizer (destructor) in C# and when should it be used?
options: It is a method (~ClassName) called by the garbage collector to release unmanaged resources when the object is collected; use only when you cannot provide deterministic cleanup via IDisposable
It is a method you call manually to free managed memory; it should be used for every class that allocates memory
It runs automatically when the application exits and is used primarily for logging purposes
It is invoked after Dispose() and is used to perform additional deterministic cleanup
correctAnswer: It is a method (~ClassName) called by the garbage collector to release unmanaged resources when the object is collected; use only when you cannot provide deterministic cleanup via IDisposable
explanation: Finalizers run nondeterministically during garbage collection and are intended as a safety net for releasing unmanaged resources when the consumer forgets to call Dispose.

question: What is the difference between IDisposable and a finalizer in C#?
options: IDisposable provides deterministic cleanup via a public Dispose method; a finalizer is nondeterministic and runs only when the GC collects the object
IDisposable is used only for managed resources while a finalizer is used only for unmanaged resources
IDisposable is automatically invoked by the runtime, whereas a finalizer must be called manually by the developer
IDisposable cannot be overridden, but a finalizer can be overridden in derived classes
correctAnswer: IDisposable provides deterministic cleanup via a public Dispose method; a finalizer is nondeterministic and runs only when the GC collects the object
explanation: Dispose allows the developer to release resources at a known time, while a finalizer is a fallback that the GC calls at an indeterminate moment.

question: Explain the dispose pattern in C# and why it's important for unmanaged resources.
options: It implements IDisposable, provides a protected virtual Dispose(bool disposing) method to free managed resources when disposing is true and unmanaged resources always, and suppresses finalization; this ensures deterministic release of unmanaged resources
It relies solely on try/finally blocks without implementing IDisposable, which is sufficient for unmanaged resources
It calls GC.Collect() after each Dispose call to force immediate garbage collection
It uses only a finalizer and never implements IDisposable, because finalizers are enough for cleanup
correctAnswer: It implements IDisposable, provides a protected virtual Dispose(bool disposing) method to free managed resources when disposing is true and unmanaged resources always, and suppresses finalization; this ensures deterministic release of unmanaged resources
explanation: The pattern guarantees that both managed and unmanaged resources are released correctly, allows derived classes to extend cleanup, and prevents the finalizer from running unnecessarily.

question: What is the difference between weak references and strong references in .NET?
options: A strong reference keeps an object alive and prevents it from being collected; a weak reference does not prevent collection and can be used to check if the object is still alive
A weak reference keeps an object alive while a strong reference allows it to be collected
Both weak and strong references prevent garbage collection; the difference is only in performance overhead
Weak references can only point to value types, whereas strong references can point to reference types
correctAnswer: A strong reference keeps an object alive and prevents it from being collected; a weak reference does not prevent collection and can be used to check if the object is still alive
explanation: Strong references root the object in the GC graph, while weak references allow the GC to collect the object; you can attempt to retrieve the target via TryGetTarget.

question: Explain how ASP.NET Core Web API model binding works.
options: It maps data from the HTTP request to action parameters using value providers such as route data, query string, form fields, and the request body.
It only binds data from the query string and ignores other sources.
It requires developers to manually parse JSON payloads inside the action method.
It uses reflection to generate SQL queries based on the request data.
correctAnswer: It maps data from the HTTP request to action parameters using value providers such as route data, query string, form fields, and the request body.
explanation: Model binding examines the incoming request, uses built‑in value providers (route, query, form, body, etc.) and converts the data to the types of the action parameters.

question: What is the difference between action filters and middleware in ASP.NET Core?
options: Action filters run around MVC actions and have access to the action context; middleware runs earlier/later in the request pipeline and works with raw HttpContext, not MVC specifics.
Middleware runs after MVC actions have executed, while action filters run before routing.
Action filters can only be applied globally, whereas middleware can only be applied per endpoint.
Middleware can only handle exceptions, while action filters handle authentication.
correctAnswer: Action filters run around MVC actions and have access to the action context; middleware runs earlier/later in the request pipeline and works with raw HttpContext, not MVC specifics.
explanation: Action filters are part of the MVC pipeline and can inspect/modify the action execution; middleware is outside MVC and processes the request/response before it reaches MVC.

question: Explain how ASP.NET Core implements the options pattern for configuration.
options: It binds a configuration section to a POCO class via services.Configure<T>(), then injects IOptions<T> (or IOptionsSnapshot<T>) where needed.
It requires static classes with hard‑coded values to be accessed throughout the app.
It only supports XML configuration files and uses DataSet objects for binding.
Developers must manually read configuration values each time they are needed.
correctAnswer: It binds a configuration section to a POCO class via services.Configure<T>(), then injects IOptions<T> (or IOptionsSnapshot<T>) where needed.
explanation: The options pattern uses the built‑in configuration system to map a section to a strongly‑typed class, registered with the DI container, and accessed via IOptions interfaces.

question: What is the difference between appsettings.json environments and how are they loaded in ASP.NET Core?
options: appsettings.{Environment}.json files are loaded after appsettings.json and override matching keys based on the current IHostEnvironment.EnvironmentName.
Environment files are loaded before appsettings.json, so they cannot override any values.
Both files are merged but the environment file is ignored if a key exists in the base file.
Environment files are only loaded when explicitly added in code; they are never automatic.
correctAnswer: appsettings.{Environment}.json files are loaded after appsettings.json and override matching keys based on the current IHostEnvironment.EnvironmentName.
explanation: During host building, the base appsettings.json is read first, then the environment‑specific file (e.g., appsettings.Development.json) is loaded and its values replace those from the base file.

question: Explain how the async/await state machine works internally in C#.
options: The compiler rewrites an async method into a struct/class that implements IAsyncStateMachine, tracking await points and resuming execution when awaited tasks complete.
Async/await automatically creates a new thread for each awaited operation.
The CLR dynamically modifies IL at runtime to insert continuation logic.
Async methods are compiled as ordinary synchronous methods and the await keyword is a no‑op.
correctAnswer: The compiler rewrites an async method into a struct/class that implements IAsyncStateMachine, tracking await points and resuming execution when awaited tasks complete.
explanation: The C# compiler generates a state machine that stores the method’s locals and the current state; each await yields control, and the continuation resumes the machine when the awaited task finishes.

question: What is a deadlock in async programming and how does ConfigureAwait help prevent it?
options: It occurs when an async method blocks waiting for a task that requires the current synchronization context, and ConfigureAwait(false) prevents the continuation from capturing that context, allowing it to run on a thread‑pool thread and avoid the deadlock.
It happens when two threads try to acquire the same lock object simultaneously, and ConfigureAwait(true) forces the continuation to run on the UI thread to resolve the conflict.
It is caused by recursive async calls that exceed the call stack size, and ConfigureAwait disables recursion limits.
It is a compile‑time error caused by missing async keywords, and ConfigureAwait automatically adds them.
correctAnswer: It occurs when an async method blocks waiting for a task that requires the current synchronization context, and ConfigureAwait(false) prevents the continuation from capturing that context, allowing it to run on a thread‑pool thread and avoid the deadlock.
explanation: A deadlock arises when the continuation tries to resume on a context that is blocked; ConfigureAwait(false) stops capturing the context, so the continuation can run elsewhere, preventing the deadlock.

question: What is the difference between CPU‑bound and I/O‑bound asynchronous operations in C#?
options: CPU‑bound work uses Task.Run to offload work to a thread‑pool thread, while I/O‑bound work uses async I/O APIs that free the thread while waiting for external resources.
CPU‑bound operations are always synchronous, whereas I/O‑bound operations must be declared async.
CPU‑bound tasks can only be awaited with WhenAll, while I/O‑bound tasks require WhenAny.
CPU‑bound operations block the UI thread, while I/O‑bound operations never block any thread.
